neighbours.label: Inside word-for-word stock boilerplate the model knows by heart, peaking on a small word or comma mid-passage: open-source license text (GPL 'but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty', MIT 'without restriction, including without limitation'), browser user-agent strings ('(KHTML, like Gecko)'), and book copyright notices ('No part of this publication may be reproduced, stored in a retrieval system'). Quiet for the same words (without, like, commas) in ordinary sentences and for freshly made-up legal-sounding clauses (leases, club rules). Side case: the Spanish word 'toponimia' (place-name study) also fires, weaker.
neighbours.short: inside memorized boilerplate (licenses, user-agent strings, copyright notices)
neighbours.notes: Blind test: 16 sentences written by a second author who saw only the label (blind:claude-opus-5-5 label-only), copied unedited. Solver leak (Spanish 'toponimia' top) and solver near miss placed by the blind author. Reached by play step --down from L33/N1814+ (drop -0.01, essentially none); cold labelling from own tops and probes only.
